planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; shear lightly after the first flush to encourage the second bloom.

directions: Irene Doyle is known as the 'Two Season' lavender for its unusual ability to produce two, and sometimes three, distinct flushes of deep violet-blue spikes over a single season rather than the single early-summer bloom typical of most English lavenders. It forms a dense, mounded clump of aromatic gray-green foliage and holds its flowers well above the leaves on slender stems. Shear off the spent first flush promptly to redirect energy into the second bloom cycle, and avoid heavy fertilization, which encourages foliage at the expense of flowers. Give it full sun and lean, fast-draining soil, since like other English lavenders it resents humidity and wet feet.
sources: Great Lakes Lavender Farm variety description

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in full sun with excellent drainage; naturally stays compact without heavy shearing.

directions: Lullaby Blue is a naturally compact, evergreen English lavender bred to stay small and well-shaped without regular pruning, bearing narrow gray-green leaves and sweetly fragrant spikes of lavender-blue flowers in summer. Its tidy, rounded habit suits containers, low hedging, and tight garden spaces where larger lavenders would sprawl. Grow in full sun with lean, sharply drained, neutral to alkaline soil, and avoid overwatering. Propagate by semi-hardwood cuttings rather than division to maintain the compact growth habit.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in full sun and poor to average, fast-draining soil.

directions: Martha Roderick is a dwarf English lavender selected in coastal California in the early 1980s, prized for its compact, rounded mound of powdery gray-green foliage and fuzzy, medium-purple flower spikes produced from early summer into fall. Both foliage and flowers are intensely fragrant, making it a favorite for sachets and potpourri as well as fresh and dried cut flowers. It tolerates drought, salt air, and poor soil once established, needing only full sun and sharp drainage. Deadhead after each flush to keep the plant blooming and tidy.
sources: San Luis Obispo County Garden Wise plant database
Great Lakes Lavender Farm variety description

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in full sun with excellent air circulation and sharp drainage.

directions: Mitcham Gray is a compact English lavender similar in habit to Hidcote Superior but noticeably faster to reach mature size, forming tight mounds of narrow, silvery gray-green leaves. Deep blue-violet flower spikes rise well above the foliage in a single summer flush, carrying the classic sharp, sweet lavender fragrance. Grow in full sun with lean, well-drained, neutral to alkaline soil, and shear back after flowering to maintain its dense, rounded shape and prevent the woody, open center that lavender develops with age.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in full sun and loose, well-drained soil; prune soon after flowering to maintain a tight habit.

directions: Compacta is a classic, low-growing English lavender valued for its silvery gray-green foliage and medium-purple flower spikes with violet corollas, blooming in midsummer. Its naturally dense, neat habit makes it a reliable choice for low hedges and formal edging without extensive shaping. It is the type of lavender traditionally dried for sachets, wands, and potpourri thanks to its strong, classic lavender scent. Give it full sun and loose, fast-draining soil, and shear lightly right after flowering to keep growth compact and woody stems to a minimum.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in full sun and lean, fast-draining soil; slow growing, so allow two to three seasons to reach mature size.

directions: Wee One is the most diminutive English lavender in common cultivation, forming a tight, slow-growing mound of narrow gray-green leaves topped with compact spikes of clear blue flowers and dark blue calyxes in late spring. A 2017 Plant Select introduction bred for the high-elevation Rocky Mountain climate, it combines excellent heat tolerance with outstanding cold hardiness. Its diminutive size makes it ideal for rock gardens, troughs, and the front of borders where larger lavenders would overwhelm the space. Grow in full sun with sharp drainage and avoid overwatering, which this xeric selection does not tolerate.

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun with sharp drainage; shear back by about a third in spring to force compact, bushy regrowth.

directions: Blueberry Ruffles is part of a Spanish lavender series selected for improved heat, humidity, and drought tolerance, bearing plump, blueberry-colored flower spikes with distinctly rippled, ruffled petal margins above a compact, mounded plant of fragrant gray-green foliage. It blooms early and repeats over an extended season, drawing butterflies and other pollinators. Grow in full sun in sandy to average soil that drains quickly; it tolerates neutral, alkaline, or acidic pH but not wet feet. Excellent in mixed containers and hot, sunny borders where its compact size and long bloom make it stand out from classic Spanish lavender types.
sources: Life is a Garden plant description

planting.note: Plant in spring in a sheltered, sunny spot with sharp drainage; in colder zones grow in a container and overwinter under cover.

directions: Helmsdale is a New Zealand-raised Spanish lavender hybrid noted for unusually dark, rich burgundy bracts crowning plump flower heads splashed with navy, violet, and wine tones, held above slender, upright, pale green aromatic foliage. It blooms over an exceptionally long season from spring into fall and forms a close-knit, shrubby mound. Grow in full sun in well-drained sandy or loamy soil with neutral to acidic pH, and shelter it from harsh winter wet and hard freezes, since it is less cold-hardy than English lavender types. Shear periodically to maintain its tight, robust habit and encourage continued bloom.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in full sun with excellent drainage; in zone 5 choose a sheltered site and provide winter protection.

directions: Dutch Group is a long-cultivated lavandin selection grown for its dense, silvery gray foliage and dark lavender-blue flower spikes produced over an exceptionally long season from early to late summer. As a sterile lavandin hybrid it is larger and more vigorous than true English lavenders, with a mass, ball-like silhouette when well maintained. It is noted for good cold hardiness and winter resilience compared to many lavandin cultivars, tolerating cold, wet winters better than most. Grow in full sun in average to lean, well-drained, alkaline soil, and shear after flowering to maintain its rounded form.
